name: cyber-learning-atlas index
description: Every entry in the repo with type, topic, level, source URL and date checked. Generated from entries.csv.

entries.title: T1595 Active Scanning
entries.summary: Attackers probe your internet-facing IPs to see what is open and what versions are running.

entries.title: T1566 Phishing
entries.summary: Tricking someone into clicking a link, opening a file or typing a password. Now often by text or voice call, not just email.

entries.title: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
entries.summary: Using a bug in something exposed to the internet (web app, VPN, file transfer server) to get in.

entries.title: T1133 External Remote Services
entries.summary: Logging in through a VPN, Citrix or remote desktop portal that faces the internet, often with a stolen password.

entries.title: T1078 Valid Accounts
entries.summary: Using a real username and password (stolen, bought or guessed). Hard to spot because it looks like normal work.

entries.title: T1110 Brute Force
entries.summary: Guessing passwords over and over, or trying leaked passwords on many accounts (password spraying).

entries.title: T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter
entries.summary: Running commands through a shell, PowerShell, Python and similar.

entries.title: T1053 Scheduled Task/Job
entries.summary: Setting up cron jobs or scheduled tasks so attacker code runs again later or after reboot.

entries.title: T1547 Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
entries.summary: Adding something that starts automatically at boot or login (startup items, systemd services, registry run keys).

entries.title: T1136 Create Account
entries.summary: Making a new account to keep access. On routers too.

entries.title: T1098 Account Manipulation
entries.summary: Changing an existing account (adding SSH keys, adding to admin groups) to keep or raise access.

entries.title: T1003 OS Credential Dumping
entries.summary: Pulling saved passwords or password hashes out of memory or system files.

entries.title: T1021 Remote Services
entries.summary: Using SSH, RDP or SMB with valid credentials to hop from one machine to the next.

entries.title: T1046 Network Service Discovery
entries.summary: Scanning inside the network to find other machines and open services.

entries.title: T1071 Application Layer Protocol
entries.summary: Hiding attacker commands inside normal-looking web, DNS or other traffic.

entries.title: T1572 Protocol Tunneling
entries.summary: Wrapping traffic inside another protocol (GRE, SSH, DNS) to sneak it past filters.

entries.title: T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer
entries.summary: Downloading attacker tools onto a hacked machine.

entries.title: T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service
entries.summary: Sending stolen data to cloud storage or file-sharing sites so it blends in.

entries.title: T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact
entries.summary: Ransomware: encrypting files so the owner can't use them.

entries.title: T1490 Inhibit System Recovery
entries.summary: Deleting or wiping backups and shadow copies so the victim can't restore.

entries.title: T1685 Disable or Modify Tools
entries.summary: Turning off antivirus, logging or security agents. New ID in ATT&CK v20 (it replaces the old T1562.001).

entries.title: T1195 Supply Chain Compromise
entries.summary: Breaking into a trusted vendor or open-source project so their software carries the attack.

entries.title: Using the KEV list to decide what to patch first
entries.summary: What KEV is, our 2026-11-22 counts, and how to combine KEV, EPSS and CVSS.

entries.title: Ukraine power grid attack (2015)
entries.summary: Business IT and grid control networks need hard separation.

entries.title: Equifax breach (2017)
entries.summary: Patch internet-facing systems fast, especially when a fix is public.

entries.title: SolarWinds Orion supply chain attack (SUNBURST) (2020)
entries.summary: A trusted vendor update is not proof of safety if the vendor itself is hacked.

entries.title: Colonial Pipeline ransomware (2021)
entries.summary: One old account without MFA can take down critical infrastructure.

entries.title: Log4Shell (Log4j) (2021)
entries.summary: Keep a software bill of materials (SBOM): a list of what's inside your software.

entries.title: Lapsus$ extortion attacks (2022)
entries.summary: Text-message MFA is better than nothing but is weak. Use an authenticator app or a security key.

entries.title: MOVEit Transfer mass data theft (Cl0p) (2023)
entries.summary: File transfer servers hold sensitive data and face the internet: prime targets.

entries.title: Cisco IOS XE web UI mass exploitation (2023)
entries.summary: Turn off management web interfaces on devices that face the internet.

entries.title: Microsoft Exchange Online intrusion (Storm-0558) (2023)
entries.summary: Signing keys are crown jewels. Rotate them and protect them in hardware.

entries.title: Volt Typhoon pre-positioning in U.S. critical infrastructure (2024)
entries.summary: Normal admin tools used at strange times or from strange places are the signal. You need a baseline of normal.

entries.title: Change Healthcare ransomware (2024)
entries.summary: Same lesson as Colonial Pipeline, three years later: one internet-facing login without MFA.

entries.title: XZ Utils backdoor (2024)
entries.summary: Curiosity about small weird things saves the day. Investigate the odd slowdown.

entries.title: CrowdStrike faulty update outage (not an attack) (2024)
entries.summary: Availability is part of security (the A in the CIA triad).

entries.title: Snowflake customer data theft (UNC5537) (2024)
entries.summary: Cloud accounts need MFA just like VPNs.

entries.title: Salt Typhoon and telecom router compromises (2025)
entries.summary: Routers are computers, and attackers live on them for years.

entries.title: CISA credentials leaked in a contractor's public GitHub repo (2026)
entries.summary: Never put secrets (keys, passwords, tokens) in a repo, even a "temporary" one.

entries.title: SafePay ransomware (2026)
entries.summary: Edge devices and backup servers are top targets. Patch the KEV entries for them first.

entries.title: Verizon DBIR 2026
entries.summary: Vulnerability exploitation became the top initial access vector (31%); only 26% of KEV vulns fully remediated.

entries.title: Mandiant M-Trends 2026
entries.summary: Median dwell time 14 days; exploits top vector (32%); voice phishing second (11%).

entries.title: Wireshark
entries.summary: Opens and decodes captured network traffic so you can see every packet. GitHub: wireshark/wireshark, 10.3k stars, last push 2026-11-22.

entries.title: Nmap
entries.summary: Finds hosts and open ports on a network and guesses what services are running. GitHub: nmap/nmap, 14.1k stars, last push 2026-11-22.

entries.title: Zeek
entries.summary: Turns raw traffic into clean, searchable logs (connections, DNS, HTTP, TLS, files). The analyst's favorite network sensor. GitHub: zeek/zeek, 8.3k stars, last push 2026-11-21.

entries.title: Suricata
entries.summary: An IDS/IPS that matches traffic against rules and alerts (or blocks) on known-bad patterns. GitHub: OISF/suricata, 6.9k stars, last push 2026-11-19.

entries.title: Arkime
entries.summary: Stores full packet capture at scale and lets you search sessions in a web UI. GitHub: arkime/arkime, 7.6k stars, last push 2026-11-22.

entries.title: Wazuh
entries.summary: Free SIEM and host security: collects logs, checks file integrity, flags known-bad behavior, has a dashboard. GitHub: wazuh/wazuh, 17.9k stars, last push 2026-11-21.

entries.title: osquery
entries.summary: Lets you ask questions about a computer with SQL, like `SELECT * FROM users;`. GitHub: osquery/osquery, 23.8k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: Velociraptor
entries.summary: Digital forensics and incident response: collects evidence from many machines at once with queries. GitHub: Velocidex/velociraptor, 4.5k stars, last push 2026-11-21.

entries.title: Lynis
entries.summary: Audits a Linux or macOS system and suggests hardening fixes. GitHub: CISOfy/lynis, 16.7k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: Falco
entries.summary: Watches Linux system calls and alerts on suspicious behavior, especially in containers. GitHub: falcosecurity/falco, 9.6k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: CrowdSec
entries.summary: Reads logs, spots attacks like brute force, and can block offenders. Like a modern fail2ban. GitHub: crowdsecurity/crowdsec, 15.8k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: Security Onion
entries.summary: A full free SOC in a box: Zeek, Suricata, Elastic and case management bundled together. GitHub: Security-Onion-Solutions/securityonion, 5.0k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: Sigma rules
entries.summary: A shared format for log detection rules, plus thousands of community rules. GitHub: SigmaHQ/sigma, 11.5k stars, last push 2026-11-18.

entries.title: sigma-cli
entries.summary: Converts Sigma rules into queries for a specific SIEM. GitHub: SigmaHQ/sigma-cli, 225 stars, last push 2026-11-11.

entries.title: YARA
entries.summary: Describes files by patterns so you can find matching files. Used widely in malware research. GitHub: VirusTotal/yara, 10.1k stars, last push 2026-10-27.

entries.title: Elastic detection rules
entries.license: Elastic License 2.0 (source-available, not OSI open source)
entries.summary: Elastic's public library of detection rules mapped to ATT&CK. Great for reading how pros write detections. GitHub: elastic/detection-rules, 3.0k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: Atomic Red Team
entries.summary: A library of small, safe tests that each mimic one ATT&CK technique, so you can check if your logging catches it. GitHub: redcanaryco/atomic-red-team, 12.9k stars, last push 2026-11-16.

entries.title: Invoke-AtomicRedTeam
entries.summary: The PowerShell runner for Atomic Red Team tests (works with PowerShell on Linux too). GitHub: redcanaryco/invoke-atomicredteam, 1.1k stars, last push 2025-09-08.

entries.title: Caldera
entries.summary: An automated adversary emulation platform. Now lives at apache/caldera on GitHub (the old mitre/caldera URL redirects). GitHub: apache/caldera, 7.5k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: Greenbone OpenVAS
entries.summary: Scans machines for known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. GitHub: greenbone/openvas-scanner, 5.0k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: ZAP (Zed Attack Proxy)
entries.summary: Free web app security scanner and proxy for testing websites you own. GitHub: zaproxy/zaproxy, 16.2k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: OWASP Juice Shop
entries.summary: A deliberately vulnerable online shop you run yourself, built to be hacked for learning. GitHub: juice-shop/juice-shop, 14.5k stars, last push 2026-11-22.

entries.title: Gitleaks
entries.summary: Scans git repos for accidentally committed passwords and keys. GitHub: gitleaks/gitleaks, 31.3k stars, last push 2026-10-28.

entries.title: TruffleHog
entries.summary: Finds secrets in repos and files and can check if they are still live. GitHub: trufflesecurity/trufflehog, 29.6k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: OpenSSF Scorecard
entries.summary: Grades an open-source project's security habits (branch protection, pinned dependencies and more). GitHub: ossf/scorecard, 5.9k stars, last push 2026-11-20.

entries.title: ATT&CK STIX data
entries.summary: The whole ATT&CK knowledge base as JSON. This repo's technique names come from v20.1. GitHub: mitre-attack/attack-stix-data, 728 stars, last push 2026-11-05.

entries.title: Lab 0: Build a safe lab on your Mac
entries.summary: three VMs on a private network you control, with a clean way to roll back.

entries.title: Lab 1: Map your own network with Nmap and Wireshark
entries.summary: find every machine and open service in your lab, and see what a scan looks like on the wire.

entries.title: Lab 2: Harden your Cisco 1941 router
entries.summary: lock down your router the way real network defenders do, using the same checklist that came out of the Salt Typhoon advisory.

entries.title: Lab 3: Harden a Linux VM with Lynis
entries.summary: audit your `target` VM, fix the top findings, and measure the improvement.

entries.title: Lab 4: Read login logs and catch a brute-force attack
entries.summary: see what password guessing looks like in logs, then block it automatically.

entries.title: Lab 5: Build a network sensor with Zeek and Suricata
entries.summary: watch your lab network with the two tools real SOCs use, and catch your own scan.

entries.title: Lab 6: Write your first detection rules (Sigma and YARA)
entries.summary: write one log rule and one file rule, test both, and understand every line.

entries.title: Lab 7: Endpoint visibility with Wazuh and osquery
entries.summary: run a free SIEM, connect your target VM, and catch persistence tricks like new users and changed system files.

entries.title: Lab 8: Test your defenses with Atomic Red Team
entries.summary: run small, safe tests that mimic real attacker techniques, and check whether Lab 7's Wazuh setup catches them.

entries.title: Lab 9: Hack a vulnerable web app you run yourself (OWASP Juice Shop)
entries.summary: see SQL injection and other common web bugs safely, and scan with ZAP.

entries.title: Lab 10: Build a patch plan with KEV
entries.summary: inventory the software in your lab, check it against real-world exploitation data, and decide what to fix first.

entries.title: Lab 11: Run a tabletop exercise from a real incident
entries.summary: practice incident response decisions using a real case, no computers needed.

entries.title: Lab 12: Secrets and supply chain hygiene for your own repos
entries.summary: make sure your own GitHub repos (and your AI agents) never leak keys, and learn to check software you install.
